---

The official .NET library for the Tungo Platform API (`https://api.tungo.kz`): the AI accountant, 1C integration, bank statements, e-invoices, tax forms and automations of [Tungo AI](https://tungo.kz).

It is generated from the API's OpenAPI contract, so its methods and models always match the contract it was built from.

## Requirements

.NET 8 or later, or any runtime that implements .NET Standard 2.0 (.NET Framework 4.6.2+, Mono, Unity). The `net8.0` build has no dependencies and is trimming and native AOT compatible; the `netstandard2.0` build depends on `System.Text.Json` and `Microsoft.Bcl.AsyncInterfaces`.

## Installation

```sh
dotnet add package Tungo.Sdk
```

## Quick start

```csharp
using Tungo.Sdk;

// The API key is read from TUNGO_API_KEY when it is not set here.
using var client = new TungoClient(new TungoClientOptions { CompanyId = "co_123" });

var companies = await client.Companies.ListAsync();
foreach (var company in companies.Data)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{company.Id}: {company.Name}");
}

var turn = await client.AskAsync("Which taxes are due this month?");
Console.WriteLine(turn.Answer);
```

## Authentication and configuration

Create one client and share it: it is immutable and safe to use from several threads or tasks. Every option can be passed explicitly; five of them fall back to environment variables.

| Option | Environment variable | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| API key | `TUNGO_API_KEY` | none |
| Base URL | `TUNGO_BASE_URL` | `https://api.tungo.kz` |
| Webhook secret | `TUNGO_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | none |
| Default company | `TUNGO_COMPANY_ID` | none |
| Default workspace | `TUNGO_WORKSPACE_ID` | none |
| Timeout | | 60 s (600 s for non-streaming chat turns) |
| Maximum retries | | 2 |
| Default headers, HTTP client | | none, built-in |

The API key is sent only to operations that require it; public endpoints and incoming hooks never receive it, and it never appears in error messages or debug output. Calling an authenticated operation without a key fails locally, before any request is made.

Every method also accepts per-request options: timeout, maximum retries, extra headers, an idempotency key and cancellation.

```csharp
using Tungo.Sdk;

using var client = new TungoClient(new TungoClientOptions
{
    ApiKey = "tg_...",                              // default: TUNGO_API_KEY
    BaseUrl = new Uri("https://api.tungo.kz"),      // default: TUNGO_BASE_URL, then https://api.tungo.kz
    WorkspaceId = "ws_123",                         // default: TUNGO_WORKSPACE_ID
    CompanyId = "co_123",                           // default: TUNGO_COMPANY_ID
    WebhookSecret = "whsec_...",                    // default: TUNGO_WEBHOOK_SECRET
    Timeout = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(60),             // one attempt of an ordinary request
    ChatTimeout = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10),         // one attempt of a chat turn
    StreamIdleTimeout = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(2),    // silence allowed between stream events
    MaxRetries = 2,
    HttpClient = null,                              // bring your own HttpClient (IHttpClientFactory, proxy, ...)
    HttpMessageHandler = null,                      // ... or only the handler
});

// Per request: every method takes RequestOptions and a CancellationToken.
using var cancellation = new CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30));
var company = await client.Companies.GetAsync(
    new RequestOptions
    {
        CompanyId = "co_456",
        Timeout = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10),
        MaxRetries = 0,
        Headers = new Dictionary<string, string> { ["X-Trace"] = "abc" },
        OnResponse = response => Console.WriteLine($"{response.StatusCode} {response.RequestId} {response.RateLimit?.Remaining}"),
    },
    cancellation.Token);
Console.WriteLine(company.Name);
```

`TungoClient` is thread-safe; create one and reuse it. `RequestOptions.OnResponse` receives the status, the headers, the request id and the rate-limit headers of the final response of a call.

Bringing your own `HttpClient` (`TungoClientOptions.HttpClient`): set `httpClient.Timeout = Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan` and `AllowAutoRedirect = false` on its handler. The SDK enforces its own time limit on every request; a client whose `Timeout` is shorter than `Timeout`/`ChatTimeout` of the options (the default of 100 s is) would cut chat turns, so it is refused with `TungoConfigurationException` when the `TungoClient` is created. A redirect that the client follows would carry the API key to another host: the SDK compares the origin that answered with the one it called and raises `TungoConfigurationException` instead of returning such a response.

## Errors

Every failure is a subtype of the SDK's base error. An HTTP error response becomes an API error chosen by the `error.type` field of the response body, falling back to the HTTP status when the body is not the API's error envelope:

| `error.type` | Status |
| --- | --- |
| `invalid_request_error` | 400 |
| `authentication_error` | 401 |
| `payment_required_error` | 402 |
| `permission_error` | 403 |
| `not_found_error` | 404 |
| `conflict_error` | 409 |
| `gone_error` | 410 |
| `limit_error` | 429 |
| `api_error` | 500 |
| `unavailable_error` | 503 |

An API error carries the status, type, code, message, request id, field errors, the parsed retry-after delay, the response headers and the raw body. Problems that happen without a response have their own types: connection error, timeout, decode error (a successful response whose body is not valid), and configuration or validation error (raised before any request).

```csharp
using Tungo.Sdk;

using var client = new TungoClient();
try
{
    await client.Proposals.ApproveAsync("pr_123", new ApproveRequest());
}
catch (TungoLimitException e)
{
    // 429: e.RetryAfter is the delay the API asked for.
    Console.WriteLine($"Rate limited, retry after {e.RetryAfter}");
}
catch (TungoInvalidRequestException e)
{
    foreach (var field in e.Fields)
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"{field.Path}: {field.Message}");
    }
}
catch (TungoApiException e)
{
    // Any other error status: type and code from the API, the request id for support.
    Console.WriteLine($"{e.StatusCode} {e.Type} {e.Code} {e.RequestId}: {e.ApiMessage}");
}
catch (TungoTimeoutException)
{
    Console.WriteLine("The request timed out.");
}
catch (TungoConnectionException e)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"Network problem: {e.Message}");
}
catch (OperationCanceledException)
{
    // Only when the CancellationToken you passed was cancelled.
    Console.WriteLine("Cancelled by the caller.");
}
```

All SDK exceptions derive from `TungoException`. `TungoApiException` has one subclass per `error.type` (`TungoAuthenticationException`, `TungoPermissionException`, `TungoNotFoundException`, `TungoLimitException`, ...). A missing API key or company id raises `TungoConfigurationException` before any request is sent.

`TungoDecodeException` means the server **accepted and carried out** the request (a 2xx status) but its response could not be read: the body is not valid JSON, is cut short, lacks a property the contract requires, or a streaming call was answered with something other than `text/event-stream`. It is never retried. `StatusCode`, `RequestId` and `Body` (the raw response) tell what the server did; check the effect of a write before sending it again.

## Retries and timeouts

A request is retried up to 2 times (3 attempts) on connection errors, timeouts and the statuses 408, 429, 500, 502, 503 and 504, but only when repeating it is safe: `GET`, `HEAD`, `PUT` and `DELETE` requests, and `POST` or `PATCH` requests of the operations whose contract declares an `Idempotency-Key`. For those the SDK generates a random key and reuses it for every attempt; you can pass your own. Other operations send no key, not even one you pass, because the API would ignore it.

The delay between attempts is `min(0.5 s × 2^attempt, 8 s)` with random jitter. A positive `retry-after-ms` or `Retry-After` response header overrides it; if the server asks for more than 60 s the SDK does not wait and raises the error with the delay filled in.

The timeout covers the whole request including reading the body. Streaming calls have no total timeout, only a connect timeout and an idle timeout of 120 s. Cancellation supplied by the caller is combined with the timeout.

```csharp
using Tungo.Sdk;

// For the whole client ...
using var client = new TungoClient(new TungoClientOptions
{
    MaxRetries = 5,
    Timeout = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(20),
});

// ... or for one call. A POST is retried only when it carries an idempotency key;
// the SDK generates one for the operations that accept it, or you can set your own.
var job = await client.Batches.CreateEsfPurchasesAsync(
    new EsfPurchasesJobRequest(),
    new RequestOptions { MaxRetries = 0, Timeout = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5), IdempotencyKey = "import-2025-01" });
Console.WriteLine(job.Id);
```

## Pagination

List operations use cursor pagination (`{ data, next_cursor }`). The plain method returns one typed page that knows whether there is a next page and can fetch it. The auto-paging variant is a lazy iterator: it requests the next page only when needed, carries your filters over, and stops fetching as soon as you stop iterating.

```csharp
using Tungo.Sdk;

using var client = new TungoClient();

// One page at a time.
var page = await client.Proposals.ListAsync(new ProposalsListParams { Limit = 50 });
foreach (var proposal in page.Data)
{
    Console.WriteLine(proposal.Title);
}

if (page.HasNextPage)
{
    page = await page.GetNextPageAsync();
}

// Or every item of every page; pages are fetched as the loop needs them.
await foreach (var proposal in client.Proposals.ListAllAsync(new ProposalsListParams { Limit = 50 }))
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{proposal.Id} {TungoMoney.FormatTiyn(proposal.Total.AmountTiyn)}");
}
```

## Streaming

Streaming operations use server-sent events and deliver typed events as they arrive. Leaving the loop early or closing the stream closes the connection. A stream request is retried only before its first byte; an error response is raised as the same typed API error as for ordinary calls. A chat stream that ends before its final event is reported as an error, never as a finished answer.

```csharp
using Tungo.Sdk;

using var client = new TungoClient();

// Events arrive as the model produces them; leaving the loop closes the connection.
await using var stream = client.Chat.CreateStreamAsync(new ChatMessageRequest { Message = "Summarise January" });
await foreach (var chatEvent in stream)
{
    switch (chatEvent.Value)
    {
        case ChatEventText text:
            Console.Write(text.Delta);
            break;
        case ChatEventError error:
            Console.WriteLine($"error: {error.Error.Message}");
            break;
        case ChatEventDone done:
            Console.WriteLine($"\nstop reason: {done.StopReason}");
            break;
    }
}

// Or let the SDK assemble the turn (an error event is thrown as a TungoApiException).
var turn = await client.Chat.CreateStreamAsync(new ChatMessageRequest { Message = "And February?" }).ToChatTurnAsync();
Console.WriteLine($"{turn.DialogId}: {turn.Text}");
```

`Chat.ListEventsAsync`, `Feed.ListEventsAsync` and `Batches.ListEventsAsync` return the same `TungoStream<T>`. `TungoStream<T>.GetResponseAsync()` gives the response headers (for example `X-Dialog-Id`) before the first event, and `TungoStream<T>.LastEventId` the `id` of the last server-sent event read so far. `ToChatTurnAsync()` raises `TungoDecodeException` when the stream ends without its final `done` event, so a cut connection never looks like a finished answer; the plain `await foreach` simply ends. A successful response that is not `text/event-stream` is a `TungoDecodeException`. The exception is a finished chat turn that the API replays for a repeated `Idempotency-Key` (`application/json` with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`): its stored result arrives as the events of that turn, ending with `next` (follow-ups and the next action, when it has them) and `done`.

## Webhooks

Outgoing webhooks are signed according to the Standard Webhooks specification (Svix). The verify helper takes the raw request body and the headers (`webhook-*` or `svix-*`), checks the HMAC-SHA256 signature in constant time and the timestamp within 300 s of the system clock, and returns the typed event. Any problem is reported as a webhook verification error. If no secret is passed, the client's webhook secret is used.

The send-hook helper posts an event to an incoming hook (`/hooks/{token}`) and, when given a secret, signs the exact bytes it sends in the `X-Signature: sha256=<hex>` header. The API key is never sent to hooks.

```csharp
using Tungo.Sdk;

using var client = new TungoClient(new TungoClientOptions { WebhookSecret = "whsec_..." });

// In your HTTP handler: pass the raw body and the request headers
// (ASP.NET Core: Request.Headers works as it is).
string body = "{...}";
var headers = new Dictionary<string, string>
{
    ["webhook-id"] = "msg_1",
    ["webhook-timestamp"] = "1700000000",
    ["webhook-signature"] = "v1,...",
};
try
{
    var webhookEvent = client.VerifyWebhook(body, headers);
    if (webhookEvent.Value is WebhookEventProposalWritten written)
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"proposal written: {written.Id}");
    }
}
catch (TungoWebhookVerificationException e)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"rejected: {e.Reason}"); // answer 400
}

// Sending an event to an incoming hook: the body is signed with the hook's secret;
// the API key is never sent to hook URLs.
var accepted = await client.SendHookAsync("th_...", "{\"invoice\":\"A-1\"}", secret: "hook-secret");
Console.WriteLine(accepted.EventId);
```

`TungoWebhooks.Verify` is the static form; it accepts `IEnumerable<KeyValuePair<string, string>>`, multi-valued header collections (ASP.NET Core `IHeaderDictionary`) and `HttpHeaders`, without a dependency on ASP.NET Core. Signatures are compared in constant time. A hook created with its own `signature_header` takes the signature in that header: pass `signatureHeader: "x-my-signature"` to `SendHookAsync` (or `SignatureHeader` in `AutomationsPostHookParams`).

## Money

The API expresses amounts in tiyn (1/100 of a tenge) as 64-bit integers. The money helper converts decimal strings and exact decimal values to tiyn without floating-point error, rounding half away from zero (`"1.005"` → `101`), and formats tiyn for display (`4500000` → `45 000,00 ₸`). Invalid input raises a typed error.

```csharp
using Tungo.Sdk;

long tiyn = TungoMoney.ToTiyn("1234.56");          // 123456, exact
long fromDecimal = TungoMoney.ToTiyn(1234.56m);    // 123456
decimal tenge = TungoMoney.ToTenge(tiyn);          // 1234.56
string text = TungoMoney.FormatTiyn(4_500_000);    // "45 000,00 ₸"
bool valid = TungoMoney.IsValidBinIin("123456789012");
Console.WriteLine($"{tiyn} {fromDecimal} {tenge} {text} {valid}");
```

Amounts in models are `long` tiyn. `ToTiyn(double)` exists for convenience and goes through the shortest round-trip decimal form of the value.

## Models

Every schema of the contract is a `sealed record` with `init` properties; properties the contract requires are C# `required` members. A response body that lacks a required property or holds a value of the wrong type fails with `TungoDecodeException`. Stream events, webhook events and error details are read tolerantly: there a required property the server did not send is left at its default value (`null` for a reference type) instead of ending the stream. Unknown JSON properties are kept in `AdditionalProperties`. Enumerations are string-backed structs: a value this SDK version does not know is preserved (`IsKnown` is false) instead of failing. Unions expose `Value` for pattern matching and keep an unknown variant as raw JSON (`IsUnknown`, `Json`).

A `PATCH` body can tell "leave unchanged" from "set to null":

```csharp
using Tungo.Sdk;

using var client = new TungoClient();

// Optional<T> tells "leave unchanged" (not set) from "clear" (explicit null).
var endpoint = await client.Webhooks.UpdateEndpointAsync("ep_123", new WebhookEndpointPatch
{
    Description = "Orders",                               // change
    EventTypes = null,                                    // send "event_types": null
    // Channels is not set: the property is not sent at all
});
Console.WriteLine(endpoint.Id);
```

## Waiting for long operations

```csharp
using Tungo.Sdk;

using var client = new TungoClient();

var run = await client.RunScenarioAndWaitAsync(
    "sc_123",
    wait: new TungoWaitOptions { Timeout = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5) });
Console.WriteLine(run.State.IsKnown ? run.State.Value : $"new state: {run.State.Value}");

var batch = await client.WaitForBatchAsync("bt_123");
Console.WriteLine(batch.Running);
```

The helpers poll with a growing interval and raise `TungoTimeoutException` when `TungoWaitOptions.Timeout` passes.

## Versioning and support

This library follows [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/). While the major version is 0, a minor release may contain breaking changes; they are always listed in the [changelog](https://github.com/TungoAI/tungo-sdk-dotnet/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). This README describes version 0.3.0.

The code is generated: please report problems and ideas in the [issue tracker](https://github.com/TungoAI/tungo-sdk-dotnet/issues) rather than opening pull requests against generated files. To report a vulnerability, follow the [security policy](https://github.com/TungoAI/tungo-sdk-dotnet/blob/main/SECURITY.md).
